title: Deterministic NP-hardness reductions for Euclidean SVP
status_note: Bennett explicitly posed this exact-or-approximate deterministic Karp-hardness question in January 2023. Wan’s arXiv 2603.27398v3 (22 July 2026) states a positive solution covering exact Euclidean GapSVP, and Hirahara–Ogitsuka’s 9 September 2026 conference paper independently describes that range as unconditional deterministic polynomial-time many-one hardness. The present review checked the matching theorem, explicit construction, projection argument, parameter and reduction-time chain, and key stated arithmetic dependencies; it did not formally verify the full proof or reconstruct its underlying cohomology. Wan’s work is a preprint in the checked record. The separate August preprint’s corrected tensor argument is not needed for this exact endpoint. This review supports a resolved disposition for the original exact endpoint, subject to the stated proof-audit limits; it does not assert peer-reviewed publication of the underlying hardness manuscript.

title: Exact counting of linear extensions below base two
status_note: Resolved affirmatively by a checked preprint: Oka, arXiv:2608.19505v1 (19 August 2026), Theorem 1 gives deterministic exact O*(1.89^n) counting for arbitrary n-element posets. On 16 September 2026 this review read the original Dagstuhl question and the complete proof in §§2–5, checked profile decoding, deadline-state aggregation and total state counts, and verified both base inequalities by exact integer/rational arithmetic. The author verifier passed on all 5,231 naturally labeled posets of orders one through six, 100 random cases and 120 targeted cases. Finite tests support but do not replace the proof. This is an arXiv preprint, not represented as peer reviewed, and no Lean proof was checked. A polynomial overhead is absorbed by a fixed slightly larger base still below two, answering the original O(c^n) existence question.

title: Tarski fixed-point search belongs to CLS and EOPL
status_note: Resolved affirmatively for both classes. The source proves the same totalized circuit problem lies in PLS ∩ PPAD; the full-version proofs of Theorems 3.2–3.3 and Corollary 3.4 were read. Fearnley–Goldberg–Hollender–Savani (STOC 2021, Theorems 6.1/6.4) give CLS = PLS ∩ PPAD, and Göös et al. (CCC 2022, Theorem 1) give EOPL = PLS ∩ PPAD and explicitly state the Tarski consequence. The latter’s definition equivalence and main reductions were checked. Thus neither source membership alternative remains open. This review is not a claim of a new independent proof or an existing Lean formalization.

title: Nonadaptive quantitative group testing
status_note: Resolved affirmatively for the user-selected count-valued subset-query target with unrestricted decoding. On 16 September 2026 this review inspected Feige and Lellouche, arXiv:2006.09074v1, §1 and Appendix A.3 Lemma 13, pp. 35–36: its pools form a binary Bernoulli matrix, and its growing-sparsity information-theoretic upper bound gives O(k) tests for every fixed power-law exponent. The full upper-bound argument was checked for the required model; the preprint is not represented as a peer-reviewed publication. The earlier Grebinski–Kucherov report was also inspected but its explicitly fixed-sparsity theorem is not alone used for the growing regime. Later multiset-query efficient-decoding results are distinguished. No polynomial decoding-time requirement was stated by the selected question, and this status makes no assertion that all efficient subset-decoding variants are resolved. No new mathematical theorem or Lean formalization is claimed.
